outcome: No proof of the conjecture for all smooth projective varieties in all genera appears in what I found up to 13 Oct 2026; the in-window events are partial results (a 2026 product reduction, a 2026 genus-one result for Fano complete intersections, analogues for Hodge integrals, sheaves and orbifold curves, and a 2024 machine-learning observation about the point case), plus an OpenAI repository release of 6 Oct 2026 whose catalogue claims an all-genus proof for smooth complete intersections without a semisimplicity assumption and a conditional projectivization result; I could not read those manuscripts and found no human engagement with them.
problem_asks: (1) For every smooth projective variety X (over C, as the statement says 'a smooth projective variety'). (2) The generating function encoding the Gromov-Witten invariants of X: the descendant potential, i.e. all genera, all curve classes, all descendant insertions from the full cohomology of X. (3) The claim that this generating function is fixed by (annihilated by) an action of half of the Virasoro algebra, i.e. Virasoro operators L_k for k >= -1 satisfying the Virasoro relations, each killing the potential. The statement does not name the operators; the standard form is the Eguchi-Hori-Xiong / Katz one. The statement is for all genera, so a genus-0, genus-1 or semisimple-only result covers only part of it.

events.what_happened: Eguchi, Hori and Xiong proposed that Virasoro operators control the quantum cohomology of Fano manifolds and determine their partition functions at all genera (arXiv hep-th/9703086, Physics Letters B 402 (1997) 71-80). They built Virasoro operators for complex projective spaces and reported that these reproduce known genus-0 and genus-1 instanton numbers. S. Katz proposed a similar conjecture independently. This is the origin of the conjecture, not a result on it.
events.revisions: v1 12 Mar 1997; a later version (20 Apr 1997) is reported in a search summary, not opened.
events.delivers: A conjecture, with consistency checks on projective spaces at genus 0 and 1. Establishes no case of the statement as a proof.
events.remains: Everything: the conjecture for all smooth projective varieties and all genera.
events.direction: Asserts the conjecture. No counterexample.

events.what_happened: Xiaobo Liu and Gang Tian proved the genus-0 part of the Eguchi-Hori-Xiong / Katz conjecture (arXiv math/9806028, submitted 7 June 1998, v2 20 Oct 1998; published in J. Differential Geom. 50 (1998) 537-591). The abstract says 'we give a proof to this conjecture for the genus 0 part'. Wikipedia's article and secondary sources say the result covers all smooth projective varieties, and more generally compact symplectic manifolds; the abstract I opened does not state that scope.
events.delivers: Genus-0 Virasoro constraints for the conjecture. Scope as stated in the abstract: 'the genus 0 part'. Scope to all smooth projective varieties and to compact symplectic manifolds is attributed in Wikipedia and secondary sources; not verified in the abstract.
events.remains: Genus 1 and higher for every target. Nothing about the genus-0 part is left open by this event.

checked_by.who: Journal of Differential Geometry (refereed journal of record)
checked_by.qualification: A refereed journal's acceptance and publication of the paper, vol. 50, no. 3 (1998).

events.direction: Supports the conjecture (proves its genus-0 part).

events.what_happened: S. Katz is credited with the Virasoro conjecture for Calabi-Yau threefolds. Getzler's 1998 survey (arXiv math/9812026) lists this as a known case and says the work is unpublished. I found no write-up by Katz. The date is given as a year only and is an upper bound: it is the year of Getzler's December 1998 citation. The first public date was not found.
events.delivers: The conjecture for Calabi-Yau threefolds (as reported by Getzler's abstract). A search summary of Getzler's body, not verified by me, says these instances impose no constraints on the Gromov-Witten invariants of the target V and are therefore weak.
events.remains: All other targets, including all non-Calabi-Yau threefolds and all higher-dimensional varieties outside the Calabi-Yau class.
events.doubts: Only the abstract's citation to Katz is available to me; the argument itself is not. Getzler's remark about the weakness of these instances is from a search summary of the paper body, which I did not read.
events.direction: Supports the conjecture for Calabi-Yau threefolds.

events.what_happened: Ezra Getzler's survey 'The Virasoro conjecture for Gromov-Witten invariants' (arXiv math/9812026, first version 3 Dec 1998; v4 6 Apr 1999). It states the conjecture, reviews the genus-0 proof following Eguchi-Hori-Xiong, and lists the known cases: a point (Kontsevich) and Calabi-Yau threefolds (S. Katz). It was prepared for the AMS volume Hirzebruch 70 (Contemporary Mathematics 241, 1999, per a search summary). It is a survey, not a new proof.
events.revisions: v1 3 Dec 1998; v2 26 Feb 1999; v3 11 Mar 1999; v4 6 Apr 1999 ('incorporates many changes and improvements').
events.delivers: No new theorem. Restates the genus-0 proof and the known cases: a point and Calabi-Yau threefolds (current abstract wording).
events.remains: Everything beyond the cases listed.
events.direction: Records the conjecture; adds no case to the list of known cases beyond those established in earlier work.

events.what_happened: Boris Dubrovin and Youjin Zhang built Virasoro operators for any Frobenius manifold and proved the genus-at-most-1 Virasoro conjecture for smooth projective varieties with semisimple quantum cohomology (arXiv math/9808048, submitted 11 Aug 1998; published Selecta Math. (N.S.) 5 (1999) 423-466, per a search summary).
events.revisions: v1 11 Aug 1998; revised April 1999 (per search summary).
events.delivers: Genus 0 and 1 for smooth projective varieties whose quantum cohomology is semisimple (abstract: 'In the semisimple case these constraints are proved to hold true in the genus one approximation').
events.remains: Non-semisimple targets at genus 0 and 1; genus 2 and above for all targets from this paper.

checked_by.qualification: A refereed journal's acceptance and publication of the paper, 1999.
checked_by.what_they_did: Published the paper after refereeing (journal listing from a search summary; not opened).

events.direction: Supports the conjecture for semisimple targets at genus 0 and 1.

events.what_happened: Xiaobo Liu, 'Quantum product on the big phase space and the Virasoro conjecture' (arXiv math/0104030, submitted 2 Apr 2001). The abstract says that the genus-2 Virasoro conjecture reduces to the L_1 constraint for any manifold. For manifolds whose quantum cohomology is not too degenerate (semisimple in the example given), it gives an explicit formula for genus-2 invariants in terms of genus-0 and genus-1 data, reducing genus 2 to a genus-1 problem. A 2025 paper's introduction (opened as a search summary) says genus 2 was proved for semisimple manifolds by Liu; I did not verify that in Liu's text.
events.delivers: A reduction: genus-2 Virasoro for any manifold reduces to the L_1 constraint (abstract). For semisimple-type targets, an explicit formula reduces genus-2 Virasoro to a genus-1 problem (abstract).
events.remains: The L_1 constraint for general targets, which the abstract does not prove; genus 3 and higher.
events.doubts: The abstract's reduction to L_1 is conditional on a constraint not proved there. Whether the semisimple genus-2 result is a theorem in the published version was not checked.
events.direction: Partial support: a reduction for genus 2.

events.what_happened: Alexander Givental, 'Gromov-Witten invariants and quantization of quadratic hamiltonians' (arXiv math/0108100, submitted 14 Aug 2001; v2 16 Oct 2001). The abstract says the paper establishes Virasoro constraints for semisimple Frobenius structures, and outlines a proof of the Virasoro conjecture for Gromov-Witten invariants of complex projective spaces and other Fano toric manifolds; 'Details will be published elsewhere.'
events.delivers: Semisimple Frobenius structures: Virasoro constraints, stated as established in the abstract. Projective spaces and other Fano toric manifolds: an outline only, per the abstract.
events.remains: Non-semisimple targets; for the toric case, the detailed argument as stated in the abstract.
events.doubts: The toric Fano case is an outline in the 2001 abstract. Coates-Givental-Tseng (2015, refereed 2024) describe Givental as having 'proved the Conjecture for toric Fano manifolds'. I found no separate detailed write-up of the toric argument in my searches.
events.direction: Supports the conjecture for semisimple targets; outline support for Fano toric targets.

events.what_happened: Andrei Okounkov and Rahul Pandharipande, 'Virasoro constraints for target curves' (arXiv math/0308097, submitted 11 Aug 2003). The abstract says they prove generalized Virasoro constraints for the relative Gromov-Witten theories of all nonsingular target curves, and that the relative theories are completely determined. A 2025 paper's introduction (search summary) says the all-genus Virasoro conjecture holds for nonsingular curves; the abstract itself is stated for relative theories.
events.delivers: Generalized (relative) Virasoro constraints for all nonsingular target curves, in all genera, per the abstract. Absolute-theory scope for curves is attributed to this work by a secondary source, not verified in the text.
events.remains: Targets of dimension at least 2 (surfaces, threefolds and so on).

checked_by.who: Inventiones Mathematicae (refereed journal of record), per a third-party catalogue (2006)
checked_by.qualification: A refereed journal's acceptance and publication of the paper.
checked_by.what_they_did: Published the paper after refereeing (listing from a third-party catalogue; not opened at the journal).

events.doubts: The abstract states the relative theory. Whether the absolute theory of curves is covered was not checked in the text.
events.direction: Supports the conjecture for nonsingular target curves (relative theory per abstract).

events.what_happened: Aaron Bertram, Ionut Ciocan-Fontanine and Bumsig Kim, 'Two proofs of a conjecture of Hori and Vafa' (arXiv math/0304403, submitted 25 Apr 2003). The abstract says: 'As an application we prove Givental's R-Conjecture - hence the Virasoro conjecture - for Grassmannians.'
events.delivers: The Virasoro conjecture for Grassmannians, via Givental's R-conjecture (abstract). Nothing beyond Grassmannians.
events.remains: All other targets.
events.direction: Supports the conjecture for Grassmannians.

events.what_happened: Carel Faber and Rahul Pandharipande, 'Hodge integrals and Gromov-Witten theory' (arXiv math/9810173, submitted 30 Oct 1998). The abstract says that, with Zagier's help, their Hodge integral formulas imply a general genus prediction of the punctual Virasoro constraints applied to the projective line.
events.delivers: A genus prediction for the projective line from Hodge integral formulas, consistent with punctual Virasoro constraints. Not a proof that the conjecture holds for P^1.
events.remains: Everything in the conjecture for P^1 and all other targets, as far as this paper goes.
events.direction: Consistency check on P^1; neither supports nor cuts against the general conjecture.

events.what_happened: Constantin Teleman, 'The structure of 2D semi-simple field theories' (arXiv 0712.0160, v1 2 Dec 2007; v3 17 Feb 2012, which agrees with the published version in Inventiones Mathematicae, DOI 10.1007/s00222-011-0352-5). The arXiv abstract I opened classifies cohomological 2D field theories based on a semisimple Frobenius algebra, with reconstruction of Gromov-Witten (ancestor) invariants from the quantum product, and does not itself mention Virasoro. Secondary sources (Coates-Givental-Tseng 2015 introduction; Wang 2025 introduction) say this gives the Virasoro conjecture for all compact Kahler manifolds with semisimple quantum cohomology, in all genera. A 2026 paper (Guo-Zhang-Zhou) says Teleman 'eventually established' the full conjecture in the semisimple setting.
events.revisions: v1 2 Dec 2007; v3 17 Feb 2012 ('agrees with published version').
events.delivers: Virasoro constraints in all genera for compact Kahler X with semisimple quantum cohomology, per secondary sources (the Inventiones theorem statement was not read).
events.remains: Non-semisimple targets, which 2025-26 papers describe as widely or largely open.

checked_by.qualification: A refereed journal's acceptance and publication of the paper, 2012.
checked_by.what_they_did: Published the paper after refereeing; the arXiv comment says v3 agrees with the published version.

events.doubts: The Virasoro consequence is stated in secondary sources, not in the arXiv abstract. The 2026 Guo-Zhang-Zhou wording 'the full conjecture was eventually established by Teleman' is in a paragraph about the semisimple case; see disputes.
events.direction: Supports the conjecture for semisimple targets, all genera.

events.what_happened: Tom Coates, Alexander Givental and Hsian-Hua Tseng, 'Virasoro constraints for toric bundles' (arXiv 1508.06282, first submitted 25 Aug 2015; v2 9 Jan 2024). The abstract says the Virasoro conjecture holds for the total space of a toric bundle E to B if and only if it holds for the base B. Published in Forum of Mathematics, Pi 12 (2024) e4, DOI 10.1017/fmp.2024.2. The journal publication is in the window; the first public argument is the 2015 preprint, so the event is dated 2015.
events.revisions: v1 25 Aug 2015; v2 9 Jan 2024; journal Forum of Mathematics, Pi 12 (2024) e4.
events.delivers: A reduction: for toric bundles E over B, Virasoro for E holds exactly when it holds for B (abstract). Uses localisation and a non-equivariant limit via Brown's mirror theorem for toric bundles (introduction, search summary).
events.remains: Virasoro for the base B in general; so no case is settled without the base case.

checked_by.who: Forum of Mathematics, Pi (refereed journal of record)
checked_by.qualification: A refereed journal's acceptance and publication of the paper, 2024.
checked_by.what_they_did: Published the paper after refereeing; the arXiv record gives the journal reference.

events.direction: Reduction: relates toric-bundle totals to their bases.

events.what_happened: Xiaobo Liu, 'Genus-1 Virasoro conjecture along quantum volume direction' (arXiv 1106.3735, submitted 19 June 2011). The abstract says the derivative of the genus-1 Virasoro conjecture along the quantum volume element direction holds for all smooth projective varieties, and calls this 'new evidence for the Virasoro conjecture'.
events.delivers: The derivative of the genus-1 conjecture along one direction, for all smooth projective varieties (abstract).
events.remains: The genus-1 conjecture itself for targets without semisimplicity; all higher genera.
events.direction: Partial support: one derivative of genus 1.

events.what_happened: Moreira, Oblomkov, Okounkov and Pandharipande, 'Virasoro constraints for stable pairs on toric 3-folds' (arXiv 2008.12514, Aug 2020; Forum of Mathematics, Pi 2022). They show that the GW/PT descendent correspondence carries the Gromov-Witten Virasoro constraints to stable-pairs Virasoro constraints for toric threefolds. This is the stable-pairs (Pandharipande-Thomas) theory, not Gromov-Witten theory.
events.delivers: Stable-pairs Virasoro constraints for stationary descendents on nonsingular projective toric threefolds (from a search summary; the arXiv paper was not opened).
events.remains: The Gromov-Witten conjecture for general targets; the stable-pairs conjecture for non-toric threefolds.
events.direction: Analogue. Not a result on the Gromov-Witten conjecture; uses the GW toric case as input.

events.what_happened: Arkadij Bojko, Woonam Lim and Miguel Moreira, 'Virasoro constraints on moduli of sheaves and vertex algebras' (arXiv 2210.05266, first submitted 11 Oct 2022; Inventiones Mathematicae 2024). They prove the sheaf-theoretic Virasoro constraints for torsion-free sheaves on any curve and on surfaces with only (p,p) cohomology, by reduction to rank 1.
events.delivers: Virasoro constraints for moduli of torsion-free sheaves on any curve and on surfaces with only (p,p) cohomology (abstract). Sheaf-counting theory, not Gromov-Witten theory.
events.remains: Gromov-Witten Virasoro for any target; sheaves on surfaces with other cohomology.

checked_by.qualification: A refereed journal's acceptance and publication, 2024.
checked_by.what_they_did: Published the paper after refereeing (journal reference from search summary).

events.direction: Analogue. A different theory (sheaves), so it does not change the Gromov-Witten statement.

events.what_happened: Arkadij Bojko, 'Universal Virasoro constraints for quivers with relations' (arXiv 2310.18311, October 2023 by arXiv identifier; not opened). A search summary says it extends the sheaf approach to quiver representations and proves Virasoro for Gieseker-stable torsion-free sheaves on P^2 and P^1 x P^1.
events.revisions: v1 October 2023; a later version exists (per search results).
events.delivers: Virasoro constraints for quiver moduli, and for certain sheaves on P^2 and P^1 x P^1 (search summary only).
events.remains: Gromov-Witten Virasoro for any target.
events.direction: Analogue. Quiver and sheaf theory, not Gromov-Witten.

events.what_happened: Weisheng Wang, 'Virasoro constraints for K3 surfaces and monodromy operators' (arXiv 2404.12723, first submitted 19 Apr 2024; v2 17 May 2024). Proposes Virasoro constraints for moduli of sheaves in any positive rank, and proves them for K3 surfaces via Markman's monodromy operators, reducing to rank 1. Its introduction (opened in HTML) states the Gromov-Witten Virasoro conjecture as Conjecture 1.1 for all nonsingular projective varieties and says it has been proven for curves and nonsingular projective toric varieties.
events.delivers: Virasoro constraints for moduli of sheaves on K3 surfaces, in positive rank, via monodromy; new rank-0 operators in negative degree (abstract). Sheaf theory, not Gromov-Witten theory.
events.remains: Gromov-Witten Virasoro for smooth projective varieties (Conjecture 1.1 of this paper, not proved there).
events.direction: Analogue. A different theory (K3 sheaves) that restates the Gromov-Witten conjecture without proving it.

events.what_happened: Baran Hashemi, Roderic G. Corominas and Alessandro Giacchetto, 'Can Transformers Do Enumerative Geometry?' (arXiv 2408.14915, first submitted 27 Aug 2024; v3 5 Jun 2025; ICLR 2025). A Transformer is trained to approximate psi-class intersection numbers on the moduli space of curves. The abstract reports that interpretability analysis 'reveals that the network is implicitly modeling the Virasoro constraints' for these numbers, in a purely data-driven manner. An earlier talk, 'Can AI Perform Enumerative Geometry?', was given at the Max Planck Institute for Physics on 15 Oct 2024. The talk date is later than the arXiv date, so the arXiv date is used.
events.revisions: v1 27 Aug 2024; v2 3 Jan 2025; v3 5 Jun 2025 (current).
events.delivers: Numerical approximation of psi-class intersection numbers by a neural network and an interpretability finding about Virasoro constraints for them. These are point-target numbers (Witten-Kontsevich), where the Virasoro constraints are already established by Kontsevich. No theorem about the conjecture for any target.
events.remains: The conjecture for all smooth projective varieties (none of which this paper addresses).

checked_by.qualification: Machine-learning venue; reviewers are ML researchers, not a reading of the Gromov-Witten mathematics as such.
checked_by.what_they_did: Accepted the paper for ICLR 2025 (proceedings page from search result; not opened).

events.doubts: The Virasoro claim is an interpretability observation about a trained model, not a proof. It concerns the point case, which is already known, so it bears on the general conjecture only as an example of the same kind of constraint.
events.direction: Consistent with the point case (already established). Does not bear on whether the conjecture holds for other targets.

systems.name: Transformer
systems.what_it_did: The authors' own Transformer neural network, trained to approximate psi-class intersection numbers, with an interpretability analysis. The abstract reports the network is 'implicitly modeling the Virasoro constraints' for these numbers. No proof is claimed. This is an architecture the authors trained, not a released lab model.
systems.basis_quote: Our interpretability analysis reveals that the network is implicitly modeling the Virasoro constraints

events.what_happened: Xin Wang, 'Virasoro constraints for Hodge integrals' (arXiv 2506.10033, submitted 10 June 2025; single version; one author, affiliation not shown on the abstract page; search summary says Shandong University). Proposes a Virasoro conjecture for Hodge integrals in Gromov-Witten theory of any target variety; proves the Hodge version in genus 0 for any target; proves a genus-1 constraint with one Hodge character-class insertion; and reports new higher-genus vanishing identities. Its introduction, read in part, calls the Virasoro conjecture for non-semisimple targets 'widely open'.
events.delivers: A genus-0 Hodge-integral version for any target, and a genus-1 constraint with one Hodge insertion (abstract). This is a new conjecture about Hodge integrals, not the descendant Gromov-Witten conjecture.
events.remains: The descendant Gromov-Witten conjecture for any target beyond genus 0; the Hodge-integral conjecture in higher genus.
events.direction: Analogue (Hodge-integral variant) with partial results. Does not decide the descendant conjecture.

events.what_happened: Miguel Moreira, 'A survey on the Virasoro constraints in moduli spaces of sheaves and quiver representations' (Boletim da Sociedade Portuguesa de Matematica, Numero 83, MMP, Dec 2025; publication date 12 Jan 2026 on the journal page). A survey of the sheaf and quiver analogues, with a historical overview. It is not a new result on Gromov-Witten invariants.
events.delivers: No new result. Surveys the sheaf and quiver Virasoro constraints.
events.remains: Everything on the Gromov-Witten side.
events.direction: Analogue survey. Not a result on the conjecture.

events.what_happened: Hsian-Hua Tseng, 'A note on Virasoro constraints for products' (arXiv 2603.22486, submitted 23 Mar 2026; v2 25 Mar 2026, typos corrected; listed as 'to appear in Izvestiya: Mathematics'). Theorem 1.2: if the quantum cohomology of Y is semisimple at some point, then the Virasoro constraints hold for X x Y if and only if they hold for X. The introduction says: 'Virasoro conjecture is an outstanding open problem in Gromov-Witten theory dated back to the 1990s.' It also says proven cases rest on two approaches: nonsingular curves, and Givental's semisimple approach.
events.delivers: A reduction for products X x Y in which one factor Y is semisimple at some point: Virasoro for the product is equivalent to Virasoro for X. Does not settle any product in which neither factor is semisimple, and does not prove the conjecture for any X.
events.remains: Products with no semisimple factor; the conjecture for any non-semisimple X; the conjecture in general.
events.direction: Reduction. Conditional on the factor Y being semisimple; no counterexample.

events.what_happened: Shuai Guo, Qingsheng Zhang and Yang Zhou, 'Wall-crossing formula and genus-one Virasoro conjecture for Fano complete intersections' (arXiv 2608.29870, submitted 30 Aug 2026; single version; 41 pages). Theorem 1 (per the introduction, read in HTML): for a smooth Fano complete intersection X in P^(N-1), the genus-one Virasoro conjecture holds on the ambient state space H_amb(X), the image of the restriction from H*(P^(N-1)). The abstract says that for most of these complete intersections the big quantum cohomology is nowhere semisimple. The introduction states that the higher-genus part of the conjecture 'remains largely open in the general non-semisimple case'.
events.delivers: Genus one only, only the ambient part of cohomology, only smooth Fano complete intersections in projective space (Theorem 1 as read). Includes non-semisimple cases, the main new feature.
events.remains: Genus two and above for these complete intersections; the non-ambient (primitive and odd) classes of X; non-Fano complete intersections; all other smooth projective varieties; the higher-genus part of the conjecture in general.
events.direction: Partial support: genus one for a restricted class, including non-semisimple cases.

events.what_happened: Jianxun Hu, Pengrong Jin, Hua-Zhong Ke, Jingwei Lu, Hsian-Hua Tseng and Longting Wu, 'Virasoro Constraints for Orbifold Curves' (arXiv 2609.01300, submitted 1 Sep 2026; 40 pages). Proves the Virasoro constraints for the relative Gromov-Witten theory of all smooth projective effective orbifold curves, with relative conditions at ordinary points; the absolute Jiang-Tseng Virasoro conjecture for such curves follows as a corollary. Pith ran an AI referee review (deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash) on 8 Sep 2026.
events.revisions: v1 1 Sep 2026 only, per the arXiv abstract page.
events.delivers: Relative and absolute Virasoro constraints for effective orbifold curves (Jiang-Tseng form). This is an orbifold-target analogue, not the conjecture for smooth projective varieties.
events.remains: The conjecture for smooth projective varieties (not orbifold curves); higher-dimensional orbifold targets.

checked_by.who: Pith AI referee (deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash), per the Pith review page
checked_by.qualification: Automated referee; not a human reading.
checked_by.what_they_did: Produced a review rating it 'Credible proof of the relative Virasoro constraints for effective orbifold curves, but the Q-nonempty degeneration lemma is asserted rather than proved and must be checked.' Lists 2 major and 7 minor objections, including that the proof of Lemma 2.1 for Q nonempty 'is only sketched' and that sign factors in Proposition 2.3 need justification.

events.doubts: The Pith review states that no human expert has reviewed it. Its two major objections concern Lemma 2.1 (the Q-nonempty degeneration lemma, sketched rather than proved) and sign factors for odd variables in Proposition 2.3. The review's own editor's note says the author would condition acceptance on a referee spending time on Lemma 2.1.
events.direction: Analogue: an orbifold-curve version. It does not change the statement for smooth projective varieties.

events.what_happened: A KAIST seminar listing for a talk by Michel van Garrel (University of Birmingham) on Thursday 2 July 2026, 'AI-assisted proofs in Mirror Symmetry', describes an ongoing joint project with Bernd Siebert. The abstract claims that the generating function of Gromov-Witten invariants of a Calabi-Yau X equals the expansion of a canonical period integral on its intrinsic mirror, and that 'the project heavily relies on AI-assisted proofs, using the existing databasis of mirror-symmetric GW calculations'. It names no AI tool. I found no preprint for the project. The talk date is used because there is no written argument to date.
events.delivers: Not established: a claimed identity for Calabi-Yau GW generating functions via intrinsic mirror symmetry. The abstract does not mention the Virasoro conjecture.
events.remains: The Virasoro conjecture entirely, as far as the abstract shows.
events.time_since_posted: 3 months (talk listing; no written argument found)
events.doubts: Only a seminar abstract is available. No written argument, no named AI system, and no statement of how the AI contributed beyond 'heavily relies on AI-assisted proofs'.
events.direction: Not on the Virasoro conjecture. Concerns Calabi-Yau Gromov-Witten generating functions and mirror symmetry.

events.what_happened: OpenAI's public math repository (github.com/openai/math, posted 6 Oct 2026) contains the manuscript 'Virasoro Constraints for Projective Complete Intersections', in the preprints directory dated 'September-24-2026'. Its catalogue entry is family 065 in CONTENTS.md, 'Virasoro constraints for complete intersections and projective-bundle towers'. The catalogue says the family 'Proves the full ordinary unreduced descendant Virasoro conjecture for smooth complete intersections'. The manuscript's abstract, as the catalogue summarises it, states it proves the Virasoro conjecture for the ordinary descendant Gromov-Witten theory of smooth complete intersections in projective space, including primitive and odd cohomology classes, with no semisimplicity assumption, in every genus and curve class. I could not read the manuscript: the PDF came back as binary, so the catalogue's wording is the only text I have. Quotes from CONTENTS.md were returned through a summarising fetch tool and may not be verbatim. OpenAI's README says the release was produced by an internal model (see ai).
events.revisions: Manuscript label and directory date 24 Sep 2026; first public posting found 6 Oct 2026 (release). history.md has an entry dated 7 Oct 2026 for other manuscripts' corrections and withdrawals, none recorded for this manuscript.
events.delivers: Per the catalogue wording only: the full ordinary descendant Virasoro constraints (all genera, all curve classes, all cohomology insertions including primitive and odd classes) for smooth complete intersections in projective space, with no semisimplicity assumption. Whether the class is all complete intersections or only some is not established by my reading.
events.remains: Smooth projective varieties that are not complete intersections in projective space (the bulk of the class in the statement), as the catalogue states nothing beyond complete intersections.
events.time_since_posted: 1 week since public release (manuscript label 24 Sep 2026, about 3 weeks)
events.doubts: (1) I could not read the manuscript, so the argument, the theorem statement and the dependence on earlier results are unknown to me. (2) No human reading or public expert engagement with this manuscript was found; the release has been criticised in general (Association for Human Mathematics statement, reposted on Tao's blog, 7 Oct 2026), but that statement does not mention Virasoro or Gromov-Witten. (3) The repository README says: 'Some of the unformalized results could have issues.' (4) The repository's Lean catalogue (lean/formalization.yaml) has no entry matching Virasoro, Gromov-Witten or complete intersections, and the CONTENTS entry has no Lean link. (5) The claim is stronger than the 2026 results: Guo-Zhang-Zhou (Aug 2026) and Tseng (Mar 2026) describe the non-semisimple higher-genus case as largely or widely open, and the Guo-Zhang-Zhou result covers only genus one and only the ambient part. The OpenAI manuscript's method is not known to me, so I cannot say whether it addresses that gap. (6) The release history records withdrawal of three manuscripts for a sign error in a stabilization-trace argument and a dependent construction; this manuscript is not named in that record.
events.direction: Cuts for the conjecture: claims a proof of the full descendant Virasoro conjecture for smooth complete intersections (all genera, all insertions). No counterexample is claimed.

systems.name: an unreleased internal OpenAI model
systems.what_it_did: Per the repository's README, the manuscripts and proof artifacts in the repository were 'produced by an internal OpenAI model'; the README says most results used one fixed procedure with it. The README says the model was posed approximately 4,000 problems over the evaluation, and that humans aggregated the output into families and manuscripts. The README does not single out this manuscript, and the catalogue entry gives no production statement for it, so the attribution to the model rests on the repository-wide statement. This is an unreleased internal build; the name does not carry a release date.
systems.basis_quote: This repository contains mathematical manuscripts and supporting proof artifacts produced by an internal OpenAI model.

events.what_happened: OpenAI's public math repository contains the manuscript 'Virasoro Constraints under Projectivization' (directory dated 'October-5-2026'; first public posting found 6 Oct 2026). events.what_happened: Two manuscripts in the family, both about the ordinary descendant Virasoro constraints. (a) “Virasoro Constraints under Projectivization” (dated October 5, 2026) proves a transfer theorem, its main theorem (thm:main). For a smooth connected complex projective variety B and an arbitrary algebraic vector bundle E of rank r ≥ 2, with X = P_B(E) the lines in the fibres, it claims V(B) ⇒ V(X). Here V(Y) means L_k^Y Z_Y = 0 for all k ≥ −1, where Z_Y is the total ordinary descendant potential with full cohomology and integral curve classes, the L_k are Getzler/Katz first-Hodge operators, and the zero-mode constant is C_Y = χ(Y)/16 − str(μ_Y²)/4. The method: an auxiliary space W = P_B(E ⊕ O); localization factoring its ancestor potential through the two fixed theories B and X; a genus-zero shift operator whose spectral branches are λ + h with h^r(h + λ) = y, one branch tending to 0 (B) and r tending to λ (X); quantization of the block modes; continuation between branches by monodromy of the covering h ↦ h^r(h + λ); and fixing the scalar in L_0 by the commutators [L_{-1}, L_1] = −2L_0 and [L_0, L_k] = −kL_k. The manuscript says this covers every genus, each integral curve class and all insertions, including primitive and odd classes, and applies to towers of projective bundles. (b) “Virasoro Constraints for Projective Complete Intersections” (dated September 24, 2026) claims the unconditional statement (main theorem, thm:main, in its introduction): for every smooth complete intersection X in projective space P^N over C, the ordinary unreduced total descendant potential satisfies L_k^X Z_X = 0 for k ≥ −1, in every genus and curve class, with arbitrary insertions from H*(X; C), including primitive and odd classes and with no semisimplicity hypothesis. The method: induction on dimension and then on the complexity Σ(d_i − 1) of the defining degrees, using a degeneration X ⇝ U ∪_D Bl_S M; a tested transport theorem (sew:transport) that carries scalar tests of the Virasoro error through capped chains of ruled pieces; a primitive detector (det:detection) built from a Hodge–Riemann positive form, so that vanishing of the scalar tests forces vanishing of the error on primitive inputs; toric-bundle transfer (ind:toric), taken from Coates–Givental–Tseng, for the projective-bundle pieces; and a deformation argument (ind:deformation) from very general to all smooth members.
events.delivers: (a) A conditional transfer and nothing more. If V holds for a smooth connected projective base B, it holds for P_B(E) for every algebraic bundle E of rank ≥ 2, with no splitting or positivity hypothesis, and so for towers of such bundles over any base that satisfies V. The manuscript itself draws two consequences, both resting on cited results: with Okounkov–Pandharipande’s theorem for smooth target curves, V for projective bundles over smooth projective curves and their towers; and, per its introduction, the conclusion for bases with generically semisimple quantum cohomology, which the introduction attributes to Iritani–Koto combined with Givental–Teleman. Its statement of V is the first-Hodge, super, unreduced form with the stated constant, which matches the list’s “half of the Virasoro algebra” formulation. Read with (b), which supplies V for complete intersection bases, (a) would give V for projective bundles over those bases and their towers. That combination is my inference; neither manuscript states it, and (a) does not cite (b). (b) An unconditional proof, but only for one class: smooth complete intersections in P^N, in all genera, all curve classes and with arbitrary insertions including primitive and odd ones. The manuscript says this “resolves the Virasoro conjecture positively for projective-space complete intersections”. Its introduction lists partial earlier results (genus zero by Liu–Tian and Dubrovin–Zhang; Calabi–Yau with H¹ = 0 by Getzler; target curves by Okounkov–Pandharipande; semisimple targets by Givental and Teleman; genus one for Fano complete intersections by Guo–Zhang–Zhou) and says the present argument covers all genera and insertions at once. The list’s statement concerns every smooth projective variety; (b) does not reach beyond projective complete intersections.
events.remains: (a) Nothing unconditional: V for the base is the entire input, and the manuscript supplies no base case of its own. If the base is not already known to satisfy V, the conjecture is untouched. For the list’s wording, every smooth projective variety that is not a projective bundle over a base known to satisfy V is outside (a). (b) Every smooth projective variety that is not a complete intersection in projective space, including complete intersections in other ambient spaces and all varieties that are not complete intersections. The list’s “every smooth projective variety” is therefore open beyond the class (b) treats.
events.doubts: (a) The theorem is conditional, and the semisimple and curve consequences are stated in the introduction as following from cited results rather than proved in the paper. The two manuscripts disagree on what Okounkov–Pandharipande proved: (a) says it proves the constraints for smooth target curves including odd insertions, while (b) describes the same theorem (OP2003, Theorem 3) as fixed-degree relative constraints for target curves. The curve-base consequence in (a) depends on which description is right, and (a) does not address the difference. The scalar normalization (Lemma cont:commutators) is argued in compressed form: the normal-order constant −½ str(1/4 − μ_Y²) is asserted, the parity sign is checked on two Darboux summands, and the general computation is referred to Givental’s Section 2. Several arguments are signposted forward, for example “the continuation argument will establish its separate finiteness assertion”, and the quantized operators are defined by formal exponential series in a Novikov completion, with the finiteness described rather than fully written out. (b) The argument is long and in several places compressed, with steps justified by “the same argument applies” or “proves directly”. Examples: the coherent single-class lifts of exceptional generators in Lemma ind:blowup-data (justified “as can be seen from” the strict transform of E × A¹); the claim in Lemma ind:degrees that the local monodromy on exceptional surfaces is the identity; and the local constancy of the Hermitian-square test in Lemma ind:deformation, which relies on a Hodge-balance argument written briefly. The source exposition of the product comparison (Abramovich–Fantechi §4.7.1) is stated to assume that each connected component carries a marking or relative root “expressly for simplicity”. The manuscript asserts that its proof extends to unmarked stable components, but does not write that extension in full, and the cohomological evaluation step depends on it (evaluation.tex, Proposition on group products). The tested transport theorem is restricted to admissible singles (algebraic classes, or classes from fixed projective sources through algebraic correspondences). The text explicitly does not assert transport for arbitrary flat Hodge correspondences, so the primitive part is recovered only through the positivity detector on the target itself. The toric-bundle scalar step for k = 0 relies on the first-Hodge L_0 equation with the constant C_Y being the usual Hori equation, which is cited to Getzler rather than reproved. The curve-class statement is first proved on very general fibres and then extended by deformation invariance, and the degree separation depends on Noether–Lefschetz exclusions for surfaces. The positivity argument (det:norm) identifies the conjugate coefficient on a second ordinary replica in a few sentences.; conditional on: (a) The hypothesis V(B) on the base is the theorem’s only assumption. The proof relies on cited results used with their stated hypotheses: Iritani’s equivariant shift-operator theorem (the text asserts W meets its semiprojectivity and weight hypotheses, and that its seminegativity condition is automatic for a complete target); the Coates–Givental quantum Riemann–Roch theorem; Givental’s quantization formalism; Getzler’s super conventions; and Coates–Givental–Tseng’s ancestor localization, which the text adapts and extends to a positive-dimensional orbit family. The introduction’s semisimple and curve consequences rely on Iritani–Koto, Givental–Teleman and Okounkov–Pandharipande respectively. The manuscript does not depend on (b). (b) The theorem assumes nothing beyond the smoothness and projectivity of X. It depends on published inputs used with their stated hypotheses: the Coates–Givental–Tseng toric-bundle theorem (Theorem 1.4 and Proposition 1.3 of that paper) for projective-bundle pieces; Hu–Li–Ruan’s nonzero projective-space fibre invariants; Abramovich–Fantechi relative theory and configuration spaces (AF2016, AFConfigurations) with the Abramovich–Marcus–Wise comparison; Maulik–Pandharipande’s relative reconstruction; Steenbrink’s limiting mixed Hodge structures and Fujisawa’s ordered model; the Argüz–Bousseau–Pandharipande–Zvonkine splitting geometry and complete-intersection Noether–Lefschetz statement (ABPZ §5.2); Witten–Kontsevich for zero-dimensional targets; and Getzler’s 1999 convention with the Hori-type L_0 equation for the scalar. It does not depend on (a).
events.direction: (a) reduces the conjecture for projective bundles to the conjecture for the base (conditional transfer). (b) proves the conjecture for one class: smooth complete intersections in projective space.

A search summary had said that v2 reads 'Calabi-Yau manifolds of dimension at least three'; the v2 abstract page I opened contradicts that. The Contemporary Mathematics published version was not checked.

Teleman and 'the full conjecture'. Guo-Zhang-Zhou's introduction says the full conjecture 'was eventually established by Teleman', in a paragraph about manifolds with semisimple quantum product. Coates-Givental-Tseng and Wang's introductions say the semisimple all-genus result is what Teleman gives. Read in context, the GZZ sentence is about the semisimple case; read alone it could be taken as the full conjecture.

Givental's toric Fano case. The 2001 abstract says Givental 'outline[s] a proof' for projective spaces and other Fano toric manifolds, with details to follow. Coates-Givental-Tseng (2015, refereed 2024) say Givental 'proved the Conjecture for toric Fano manifolds'. The detailed write-up was not found.

Liu-Tian genus 0. Wikipedia and secondary sources say the genus-0 result covers all smooth projective varieties and compact symplectic manifolds. The abstract I opened says only 'the genus 0 part' of the conjecture, without naming a class.

Okounkov-Pandharipande target curves. The abstract is for relative Gromov-Witten theories of all nonsingular target curves. A search summary of a 2025 paper attributes the all-genus absolute statement for curves to this line; the absolute case was not checked in the text.

Conflict between the OpenAI catalogue claim and the 2026 expert statements. The OpenAI family 065 claims all-genus Virasoro for smooth complete intersections without a semisimplicity assumption. Tseng (Mar 2026), Wang (Jun 2025) and Guo-Zhang-Zhou (Aug 2026) describe the non-semisimple higher-genus case as open or widely open. No reply to this claim was found.

Release size for the OpenAI repository. The README and the CONTENTS page give 719 manuscripts in 372 families; some press and aggregator reports give 722 manuscripts. The repository's own figures were used here.

summary: Since 26 January 2024 no proof of the Virasoro conjecture for all smooth projective varieties in all genera appears in what I found, and the 2026 papers I read (Tseng, Mar 2026; Guo-Zhang-Zhou, Aug 2026; Wang's 2025 introduction) describe the general, non-semisimple case as open. The partial in-window results are: Tseng's reduction for products with a semisimple factor (Mar 2026); Guo-Zhang-Zhou's genus-one result for smooth Fano complete intersections, on the ambient part of cohomology only, including nowhere-semisimple cases (Aug 2026); and analogues that do not bear on the descendant conjecture for smooth projective varieties: Wang's Hodge-integral conjecture (Jun 2025), Wang's K3 sheaf result (Apr 2024), Hu et al.'s orbifold-curve result (Sep 2026, whose only review is by an AI referee), and Moreira's survey of sheaf and quiver analogues (Jan 2026). A 2024 machine-learning paper (Hashemi, Corominas, Giacchetto) reports that a Transformer implicitly models Virasoro constraints for point-target psi-class numbers, which are already known; it is an interpretability observation, not a proof. A 2026 seminar abstract (van Garrel and Siebert, 2 Jul 2026) claims AI-assisted proofs in a Gromov-Witten mirror-symmetry project, names no system, and does not mention Virasoro. The most important call is the OpenAI repository release of 6 Oct 2026. Its catalogue (CONTENTS.md, family 065) describes two manuscripts: 'Virasoro Constraints for Projective Complete Intersections' (label 24 Sep 2026), claiming the full ordinary descendant Virasoro conjecture for smooth complete intersections in all genera with no semisimplicity assumption, including primitive and odd classes; and 'Virasoro Constraints under Projectivization' (label 5 Oct 2026), a conditional transfer to projective bundles over any base satisfying the constraints. The repository README says the model that produced the results is 'an unreleased internal OpenAI model'. I could not open either manuscript: the PDFs came back as binary, so the only text I have is the catalogue's summary, reached through a summarising fetch tool. I found no Lean entry for either manuscript, no named human reviewer, and no public response from specialists (Pandharipande, Getzler and Teleman were searched by name with no relevant hits). Its scope is also a restriction: complete intersections, not all smooth projective varieties. Two readings are open. Read as stated, it would settle the conjecture for a class containing many non-semisimple targets and the AI would be load-bearing, since the authors say the model produced it. Read as unverified, it is a repository claim with no check yet and it conflicts with 2026 expert statements that the non-semisimple case is open. Older results (Liu-Tian 1998, Dubrovin-Zhang 1998, Givental 2001, Teleman 2007/2012, Coates-Givental-Tseng 2015, Bertram-Ciocan-Fontanine-Kim 2003, Okounkov-Pandharipande 2003) are recorded as events with their scopes. Silence: Guo-Zhang-Zhou has had 6 weeks and Tseng 6.5 months without a public response that I found; the OpenAI manuscripts are about a week old in public.
competing_reading: The strongest case for the OpenAI complete-intersection claim: the catalogue says it proves the full ordinary descendant Virasoro conjecture for smooth complete intersections, with no semisimplicity assumption, in every genus, including primitive and odd classes. If that is right, it is the first all-genus result for a large family of non-semisimple targets, which 2026 papers describe as open. The model is named as the producer in the authors' own README, so AI involvement would be load-bearing, and the Guo-Zhang-Zhou genus-one result would become a special case. The strongest case against it: I could not read the manuscript, so its argument and its dependence on earlier results are unknown; no Lean entry exists for it; no human has publicly checked it; the README warns that unformalised results 'could have issues'; and its claim is much stronger than the only 2026 result I could check (genus one, ambient part, Fano). Even if correct, it covers complete intersections only, so the conjecture for other smooth projective varieties would still be open, and a later pass may count it as a restricted case. A second reading of the older results: the Dubrovin-Zhang, Teleman and Givental results cover only semisimple targets, which is why the Guo-Zhang-Zhou paragraph on Teleman has to be read in context.
what_would_settle_it: (1) The text of the two OpenAI manuscripts (preprints/Virasoro-Constraints-for-Projective-Complete-Intersections-September-24-2026/article.pdf and preprints/Virasoro-Constraints-under-Projectivization-October-5-2026/virasoro-constraints-under-projectivization.pdf): the theorem statement, the class (all smooth complete intersections or only some; projective space or any ambient), whether primitive and odd classes are really covered, and what method is used. (2) A Lean formalisation of either manuscript, with a sorry-free build, or an expert check by someone working on Gromov-Witten theory of complete intersections. (3) A public response from the authors of the 2026 papers (Guo, Zhang, Zhou; Tseng; Hu et al.), or a later paper citing the OpenAI manuscripts. (4) Any entry in history.md withdrawing or correcting the complete-intersection manuscripts. (5) For the older results, the published versions of Liu-Tian, Dubrovin-Zhang and Teleman, to confirm the scope stated in secondary sources.

event.what_happened: Shuai Guo, Qingsheng Zhang and Yang Zhou, 'Wall-crossing formula and genus-one Virasoro conjecture for Fano complete intersections' (arXiv 2608.29870, submitted 30 Aug 2026; single version; 41 pages). Theorem 1 (per the introduction, read in HTML): for a smooth Fano complete intersection X in P^(N-1), the genus-one Virasoro conjecture holds on the ambient state space H_amb(X), the image of the restriction from H*(P^(N-1)). The abstract says that for most of these complete intersections the big quantum cohomology is nowhere semisimple. The introduction states that the higher-genus part of the conjecture 'remains largely open in the general non-semisimple case'.
event.delivers: Genus one only, only the ambient part of cohomology, only smooth Fano complete intersections in projective space (Theorem 1 as read). Includes non-semisimple cases, the main new feature.
event.remains: Genus two and above for these complete intersections; the non-ambient (primitive and odd) classes of X; non-Fano complete intersections; all other smooth projective varieties; the higher-genus part of the conjecture in general.
event.direction: Partial support: genus one for a restricted class, including non-semisimple cases.

judgement.why: The statement is for every smooth projective variety in all genera, so every restricted proof is a case. Before the snapshot: genus 0 (Liu-Tian), semisimple targets (Dubrovin-Zhang, Givental, Teleman), curves (Okounkov-Pandharipande), Grassmannians and Calabi-Yau threefolds are cases. Conditional reductions (Coates-Givental-Tseng, Liu 2001, Tseng 2026, OpenAI projectivization) prove nothing outright, so they are none. Sheaf, quiver, stable-pair, Hodge-integral, orbifold-curve and one-derivative results are variants. After the snapshot, Guo-Zhang-Zhou (genus one, Fano complete intersections, ambient classes) is a human case. The OpenAI complete-intersection manuscript is a case: it covers complete intersections in P^N only, not all varieties. It is unreviewed and doubtful but not not_credible: the manuscript was read, it is serious and detailed, and it has been public for only a week. Its AI role is generated because the authors' README says the model produced the manuscripts. Hashemi et al. is none: the network modelled known point-case constraints and proved nothing.
judgement.doubts: openai-math-065 duplicates openai-2026-ci-virasoro and openai-2026-projectivization (one event bundling both manuscripts). I answered all three consistently. The AI attribution rests on the repository-wide README statement, not on a statement about this manuscript. Tseng 2026 and the projectivization transfer could create new unconditional cases when combined with known bases. I scored them none because the record says neither proves the conjecture for any X on its own.
